Tier assignment enforces statistical consistency between normal and lognormal models, ensuring that only propositions with aligned distributional behavior are considered reliable. The absence of market prices in inputs implies that these primitives operate in a model-relative pricing domain rather than market-relative. This creates a diagnostic-only environment where EVs are computed without reference to sharp market prices, leading to potential misalignment with actual betting outcomes. The lack of price data also precludes direct calibration against observed market behavior, necessitating reliance on internal model validation metrics such as residual-versus-close diagnostics.
